tasks.short: Put together the student's progress on marks and support-plan goals, invite parents and agree a time, meet them about progress, agree priorities and resource needs, and record them in the support plan.

steps.what: Special education teacher collects marks, support-plan goals and notes into a progress overview
Special education teacher invites parents and agrees a time by e-mail
Parents reply with a time that suits them
Special education teacher meets with parents and guardians to discuss their children's progress
Special education teacher determines priorities and resource needs together with the parents
Special education teacher records the agreed priorities in the support plan

tasks.design: The student record ({OTHER}) builds the progress overview from marks and support-plan goals by query and template, and the teacher adds context. Parents pick a slot from the teacher's open times in the parent app instead of replying by e-mail. Priorities go straight into the support-plan module with fixed fields. Meeting parents and agreeing priorities stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Overviews were pulled together by hand and times agreed in long e-mail threads.
tasks.enabler_now: Pupil record systems hold support-plan modules, goal tracking and parent apps.
tasks.still_hard: Parents disagree on priorities, and resources depend on the school's budget.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing what a parent fears behind a question about grades.

reach.learn: Whether recorded resource needs reach the coordinator sooner.

evidence.claim: ParnasSys holds pupil records, a support-plan module, learning-goal tracking and a parent app.
The support plan is set within six weeks of enrolment after consulting parents and evaluated yearly.

assumptions: Boundary: from the student record to the updated support plan; arranging resources is outside.
Input contract: marks and goals in the student record entered by teachers; open times set by the teacher; fallback is e-mail.
Parents pick a slot in the app instead of replying by e-mail; about the same time, priced as customer time.
Meeting and agreeing do not change.
research_questions: Do parents feel better prepared for the meeting?

already_counted.description: Special education teacher reads and adds to the overview.

incremental.description: Special education teacher sets open times in the parent app.
Parents pick a slot in the parent app.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: parents who do not use the app and goals kept outside the system; high: all goals in the support-plan module and most parents booking in the app.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Adapt texts and examples to students' reading levels, instruct through lectures, discussions and demonstrations, explain individually during practice, and make enlarged or simplified copies.

steps.what: Special education teacher adapts texts and examples to the students' reading levels

loop.input: The lesson text and the target reading level; no student names.
loop.output: The same text rewritten at the target level, with key terms kept.
loop.check: Code checks the key terms from the original are kept and sentence length is within the level's limit; the teacher reads every adapted text.
loop.stop: Approved by the teacher, or after two redrafts the teacher adapts it.
loop.why_not_simpler: Rewriting at a reading level needs new sentences; rules can only shorten them.

steps.what: Special education teacher instructs through lectures, discussions and demonstrations
Special education teacher explains individually during practice
Special education teacher makes enlarged or simplified paper copies

tasks.design: A bounded step rewrites lesson texts at a student's reading level and the teacher reads every result. Adapted texts go to students' laptops in the learning platform ({LMS}) with enlargement and read-aloud, so fewer paper copies are made. Instruction and individual explanation stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Texts were adapted by hand for each level and copied on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Lesson editors rewrite text at another level; laptops offer enlargement and read-aloud.
tasks.still_hard: Rewritten texts can lose the meaning the lesson needs.
tasks.human_edge: Changing the explanation mid-lesson when a student's face says it did not land.
tasks.altitude: The teacher checks adapted texts instead of rewriting them.

reach.learn: Whether adapted texts reduce help requests.

evidence.claim: LessonUp's lesson editor rewrites text at another level, summarises and translates.
In a randomised trial with 259 science teachers, a chatbot plus a guide cut weekly lesson planning from 81.5 to 56.2 minutes with no quality difference.

assumptions: Boundary: from lesson material to student copies; lesson planning is outside.
Input contract: reading levels from the student record set by the teacher; lesson material from the subject method; fallback is adapting by hand.
No student data go into the rewriting step.
research_questions: How often does the teacher reject an adapted text?

already_counted.description: Special education teacher reads each adapted text.

incremental.description: Special education teacher reports texts that lost key meaning.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: classes where most students still need paper; high: classes working on laptops with several reading levels.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare tests and adapted versions, administer them with extra time and support, mark closed items, grade open answers, and enter marks in the student record.

steps.what: Special education teacher prepares tests and assignments with adapted versions

loop.input: The base test with its answer key and the adaptation needed (larger print, fewer items, simpler wording).
loop.output: An adapted version that tests the same goals.
loop.check: Code checks each adapted item maps to the same goal and key as the base item; the teacher reads every version.
loop.stop: Approved by the teacher, or after two redrafts the teacher adapts it.
loop.why_not_simpler: Simpler wording per item needs rewriting; a template only changes layout.

steps.what: Special education teacher administers tests with extra time and support
Special education teacher marks closed items by hand
Special education teacher grades open answers to evaluate students' progress
Special education teacher types marks into the student record

tasks.design: Tests come from an item bank with an answer key per goal; a bounded step makes adapted versions that the teacher reads. Students take tests on laptops where possible, closed items are marked against the key in code, and the teacher grades every open answer. Once the teacher has finished grading, marks go to the student record ({OTHER}). No model scores open answers, since marks that count fall under the high-risk rules.
tasks.previous_blocker: Adapted versions were rewritten by hand, all items marked by hand and marks typed in.
tasks.enabler_now: Test tools mark closed items against a key and export marks to pupil records.
tasks.still_hard: Students who need paper tests keep closed items marked by hand.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing whether a wrong answer comes from the reading or the maths.
tasks.altitude: The teacher grades open answers only, not every item.

reach.learn: Whether key-marked tests speed up reporting.

evidence.claim: Texas machine-scores state tests; rescoring requests rose from 2,758 in 2024 to 64,489 in 2026, and computers first scored 58% of over 13,300 raised reading scores.
AI that evaluates learning outcomes is high-risk under Annex III point 3 from 2 December 2027.

assumptions: Boundary: from learning goals to marks recorded; report cards are outside.
Input contract: item bank and keys kept by the subject section; learning goals from the support plans; fallback is paper tests.
Administering and grading open answers do not change.
Closed-item marking uses a fixed key, not a model.
unknowns: Share of tests taken on laptops.
research_questions: Do adapted versions measure the same goals?

already_counted.description: Special education teacher reads each adapted version.

incremental.description: Special education teacher keeps the item bank and keys current.

approvals.approved_version: The grades as finished by the teacher in s4; a changed grade needs the teacher's new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most students need paper tests; high: most tests on laptops with many closed items.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Gather results and feedback on the programme, evaluate and revise it with colleagues and administrators, draft revised sections, get approval, share the programme and follow up its use.

steps.what: Special education teacher gathers results and feedback on the current programme
Special education teacher collaborates with other teachers and administrators to evaluate and revise secondary school programs
Special education teacher writes the revised programme sections

loop.input: The revision choices, the current programme and the fixed list of core goals.
loop.output: Revised programme sections with objectives, each mapped to a core-goal code.
loop.check: Code rejects objectives without a valid goal code; the teacher edits every section.
loop.stop: Approved by the teacher, or after two redrafts the teacher writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: Revised sections need new wording; a template only gives the structure.

steps.what: Department head approves the revised programme
Special education teacher e-mails the approved programme to all staff
Special education teacher follows up how colleagues use the revised programme

tasks.design: A results view on the student record ({BI}) shows progress per group and goal, so evidence for the evaluation needs no spreadsheet work. A bounded step drafts revised sections with each objective mapped to a core-goal code, and the teacher edits them. The department head approves, and only the approved version goes to staff from the document space ({DOCS}). Evaluating with colleagues and following up stay with people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Results were exported to spreadsheets and programmes rewritten by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Pupil records feed results views; language models draft text against a fixed goal list.
tasks.still_hard: Drafting tools save time but teachers use them less after a few weeks.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which change colleagues will actually carry into their lessons.
tasks.altitude: The teacher edits drafted sections instead of writing them.

reach.learn: Whether goal-coded sections speed up approval.

evidence.claim: In a randomised trial with 464 primary teachers, a lesson assistant cut weekly preparation from 3.3 to 2.5 hours, but covered 7% of lessons and use declined over ten weeks.
A school that adapts an AI tool can become its provider under the AI Act.

assumptions: Boundary: from student results to followed-up use; national exam programmes are outside.
Input contract: results from the student record entered by teachers; core-goal list from the national curriculum; fallback is spreadsheets and writing by hand.
Evaluating with colleagues does not change.
The department head's time is outside the teacher's savings.
research_questions: Is the drafting step still used after a term?

already_counted.description: Special education teacher edits drafted sections.

incremental.description: Special education teacher keeps the goal list mapping current.

approvals.approved_version: The programme as approved by the department head in s4; any change needs a new approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: teachers stop using the drafting step after a few weeks; high: the step stays in use and results are in the record.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The special education teacher keeps instruction, parent meetings, grading open work and programme decisions; manual overviews, rewriting texts, marking closed items and typing marks shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A teacher who spends saved hours on individual help.
